suggestions.rationale: Mapping Expansion Batch ME-17 adds this relationship only as the user-approved bounded clinical proposition. The cited systematic review found a median depression prevalence of approximately one third across tinnitus patient samples, with total sample prevalence estimates ranging widely; the association direction is not established. Require independently established chronic tinnitus and a separately established depressive disorder; the cited systematic review reported frequent depressive comorbidity across tinnitus patient samples and does not establish onset order or direction. Preserve hearing loss, otologic disease, noise exposure, medications, substance use, chronic pain, and other psychiatric illness as competing explanations. Do not infer a depressive disorder from tinnitus-related distress, sleep disturbance, or impairment alone, and do not treat this population-level association as proof that tinnitus caused an individual's depressive disorder. The cited literature supports only this constrained proposition and does not, by itself, establish an individual medical nexus.

nexusClaim.associationBasis: Authoring registers this relationship only as the bounded association the located sleep literature supports: a 2022 systematic review and single-arm meta-analysis of seven studies covering 3,041 tinnitus participants reports a pooled prevalence of sleep impairment of 53.5 percent (95 percent CI 40.2-66.8) with extreme between-study heterogeneity (I-squared 97.8 percent, Q 7.90, p = 0.000), significantly higher in women than men (44.6 versus 39.1 percent, P 0.034) and varying by PSQI cut-off and sample size (PMID 34708282); a 2024 meta-analysis of seventeen adult case-control and cohort studies reports tinnitus associated with poor sleep quality alongside dementia, compromised learning, attention, anxiety and depression (all P < 0.05), with stronger associations above age 60 (PMID 38389785). The registered claim is the narrowest these anchors jointly permit: that chronic tinnitus is associated with sleep impairment at the pooled prevalence the anchors report, with the target phenotype being the SLEEP IMPAIRMENT the anchors measure and NOT a diagnosed chronic insomnia disorder, and with NO anchor establishing onset order between the tinnitus and the sleep complaint.
nexusClaim.causationStatus: Neither causation nor aggravation of chronic insomnia is established for any individual by these anchors: the primary anchor is a SINGLE-ARM prevalence meta-analysis with no tinnitus-free comparator arm, and the second pools case-control and cohort designs, so no anchor establishes that sleep disturbance follows tinnitus in time and the sleep complaint may predate, follow or share causes with the tinnitus; the anchors measure poor sleep quality by Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index and similar instruments rather than a DSM-5 or ICSD-3 insomnia diagnosis, so a pooled 53.5 percent sleep-impairment prevalence is NOT a rate of chronic insomnia and the phenotype boundary is carried on every face of the edge; the primary anchor's own regional subgroup statement is INTERNALLY INCONSISTENT, reporting non-Asia prevalence 56.6 percent (95 percent CI 42.6-70.5) as lower than Asia 34.5 percent (95 percent CI 25.7-43.3), so the labels appear transposed in the abstract and no regional inference may be drawn from it; heterogeneity is extreme (I-squared 97.8 percent). Individual claims require independently established chronic tinnitus and separately diagnosed chronic insomnia with dated onset records, exclusion of obstructive sleep apnea, restless legs syndrome and periodic limb movements, of major depressive and anxiety disorders, of hearing-loss progression and of caffeine, stimulant and medication effects before any attribution.

causalMechanism.primaryVector: A hypothesized hyperarousal pathway: persistent tinnitus signal is held to sustain auditory-limbic-autonomic arousal (thalamocortical dysrhythmia and conditioned-distress models) that raises sleep-onset latency and fragments sleep continuity, the pathway the pooled sleep-impairment prevalence is consistent with; neither anchor measures the pathway directly, so whether tinnitus produced any individual's sleep disturbance rather than mood, hearing loss or a shared arousal trait remains hypothesized until the sleep findings are read against the tinnitus and mood chronology.

evidentiaryProfile.conservativeRationale: Authored at ASSOCIATION_ONLY at systematic-review-and-meta-analysis prevalence class, following the symptom-disrupted-sleep convention the restless-leg-syndrome to insomnia edge established (batch 78) with the same instrument limits carried openly: the primary anchor is a single-arm pooled prevalence with I-squared 97.8 percent and no comparator arm, and the second anchor pools odds across outcomes and age strata. A TARGET-SCOPE DISCLOSURE is carried on the face of the edge: the catalog identity is Chronic insomnia while the anchors measure sleep impairment and poor sleep quality by PSQI-class instruments, so the evidence supports a sleep-disruption window and does not by itself meet the chronic-insomnia diagnostic standard. ONE-WINDOW-PER-CLAIM DISCIPLINE IS RECORDED: this file already holds the registered tinnitus to depressive-disorder window and the registry holds the registered insomnia to depressive-disorder window, so a tinnitus to insomnia to depressive-disorder mediation reading is plausible in the literature but NO CHAIN IS CLAIMED HERE, each window stands on its own anchors, and the depression window remains governed by its ME-17 review; the edge adds no parallel-targeting pair to the CRG redundancy question because it targets a different identity from the registered mood edge.
evidentiaryProfile.evidenceGaps: NO located anchor establishes onset order between tinnitus and the sleep complaint; the primary anchor is a single-arm prevalence meta-analysis of only seven studies with extreme heterogeneity (I-squared 97.8 percent) and no tinnitus-free comparator; both anchors measure PSQI-class sleep quality rather than diagnosed chronic insomnia; the primary anchor's regional subgroup figures are internally inconsistent (non-Asia 56.6 percent stated as lower than Asia 34.5 percent, apparently transposed); the second anchor's pooled estimates merge case-control and cohort designs and several cognitive-psychiatric outcomes, with stronger signals above age 60 that bound extrapolation to younger claimants; and no anchor reports incident insomnia in a tinnitus cohort free of baseline sleep disorder.
alternativeEtiologiesToRuleOut: Obstructive sleep apnea and other sleep-disordered breathing, which co-travels with tinnitus and with the older population the anchors weight most heavily
Restless legs syndrome and periodic limb movements of sleep as independent sleep-onset and continuity disruptors
Hearing-loss severity, noise exposure and otologic disease as the shared substrate behind both tinnitus and sleep complaint
Major depressive disorder, anxiety disorders and PTSD, whose registered windows overlap this population and which independently disrupt sleep
Caffeine, alcohol, stimulants and medication effects (including sedative-hypnotic withdrawal) and chronic pain, plus age-related sleep change

sourceReferences.citation: Gu H, Kong W, Yin H, Zheng Y. Prevalence of sleep impairment in patients with tinnitus: a systematic review and single-arm meta-analysis. Eur Arch Otorhinolaryngol. 2022 May;279(5):2211-2221. doi:10.1007/s00405-021-07092-x. PMID 34708282.
sourceReferences.note: Systematic review and single-arm random-effects meta-analysis, registered as this edge's PRIMARY anchor: seven studies, 3,041 tinnitus participants, pooled prevalence of sleep impairment 53.5 percent (95 percent CI 40.2-66.8) with I-squared 97.8 percent (Q 7.90, p = 0.000); female 44.6 versus male 39.1 percent (P 0.034); PSQI cut-off and sample-size subgroup differences reported significant. AN ERRATUM-CLASS INTERNAL INCONSISTENCY IS CARRIED: the abstract reports non-Asia prevalence 56.6 percent (95 percent CI 42.6-70.5) as LOWER than Asia 34.5 percent (95 percent CI 25.7-43.3), so the regional labels appear transposed and no regional inference is drawn anywhere on this edge. LIMITATIONS CARRIED: single-arm design without tinnitus-free comparator, seven studies only, extreme heterogeneity, PSQI-class sleep impairment rather than diagnosed insomnia. Mapping approval is not citation verification; this source enters verified:false pending separate qualified-human citation review.
